title: AC skin
caption: Air conditioning pulls moisture from the air — and from your skin's outermost layer. In a climate where you move between outdoor humidity and heavily chilled interiors all day, that cycle of dehydration and re-exposure is relentless. Dehydrated skin isn't the same as dry skin: it's a temporary loss of water content that can affect any skin type, including oily, and shows up as tightness, dullness, or fine surface lines that weren't there before. Knowing the difference means you're solving the right problem — and reaching for a humectant rather than a heavy cream. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae
